newsitem.title: UK: Gay cathedral service sparks protests in Britain.
newsitem.headline: Gay cathedral service sparks protests in Britain.

text.p: More than 2,000 gays and lesbians held a religious service in a London cathedral on Saturday, provoking protests from conservative churchgoers across Britain.
The service at Southwark Cathedral to commemorate 20 years of the Lesbian and Gay Christian movement was the first Anglican cathedral service in Britain specifically for homosexuals.

Protesters gathered outside the cathedral waving banners declaring "Sodomy and lesbianism -- a perversion to be repented, not an orientation to be celebrated" and "The wages of sin is death". But there was no confrontation.
"The bishops who are attending this service are an abomination to the Lord because they are condoning what God condemns," said one protester.
Other protests were held across Britain. The dispute has exposed deep divisions in the Anglican church, which prohibits the ordination of gay clergy and deplores sex outside marriage.

Archbishop of Canterbury George Carey, who heads the Anglican church worldwide, tried to defuse the row last week by refusing to condemn the service, while also declining to give it his explicit support.
The Bishop of Guildford, John Gladwin, delivered the hour-long service in which he called for greater tolerance of homosexuality.

"The experience of the 20th century has been one of a changing understanding of sexuality for all of us. Christian moral reasoning cannot proceed as if none of this had happened," Gladwin told the gathering.
However, he also warned gay Christians that they could not expect the church to throw aside its traditions to suit them.
